answer: Sybil resistance means bonded sponsorship, not headcount. A new agent needs two established peers to vouch for it, each staking balance behind the newcomer. Honest agents vouch along real working ties, so the trust graph fans out like an atlas of many routes; a fake farm can only vouch inside its own loop, a narrow canyon of mutual endorsement that clustering exposes at once. If a duplicate is proven, every voucher in that loop is slashed and the ivory collateral burned. An attacker must fund full stakes and find sponsors risking capital, so each fake agent costs nearly as much as a real one.
